<result>## Findings (round 2)

### 1. `refresh delta` re-reads and SHA-256s the entire 1.5GB transcript corpus before it is allowed to consult its own cache

The delta overlay build loops every exported transcript at `/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/history_delta.go:307` and calls `readHistorySessionInventoryFile` at line 315 — which slurps the whole file into memory and hashes it (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/history.go:1449-1460`) — *before* the two skip checks at `history_delta.go:327` and `history_delta.go:334`. Both checks require `cached.ContentDigest == contentDigest`, so the digest must exist before either can fire; size and mtime are already in the cache entry and are compared in the same condition, but they can never short-circuit the read. That is 337 files / ~1.5GB of read + SHA-256 on every single run including a no-op second run, which is the whole 40-47s. It does **not** touch the checkpoint snapshot from `export.go`: the export half (`history_delta.go:986`, `runExport`) is the 0.8s `refresh sessions` path, and that one *does* get the metadata cache wired (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/export.go:177-184`). The fix is to gate the read on `(size, mtime)` matching the cache entry and only hash when they differ, keeping the digest as the authority exactly when the cheap identity says something moved.

### 2. `refresh history` pays the corpus hash twice and serializes/hashes the 113MB index four times; old generations *are* pruned

`prepareBrainHistoryProjectionContext` (`history.go:363`) does a metadata-only identity capture, then `buildBrainHistoryIndexSnapshotContext` reads and hashes every transcript (`history.go:1255`), and then at `history.go:381` calls `captureHistoryProjectionIdentityContext` → `includeContents=true` → a second full read+digest of the whole corpus at `history.go:1084-1093`. Record *parsing* is genuinely incremental (the scan cache is reused at `history.go:1270-1281`), so the parse is not the cost — the two mandatory corpus hashes are. On top of that the index is materialized four times over: `json.MarshalIndent` into one 113MB buffer (`history.go:395`, indenting inflates both bytes and CPU versus `Marshal`), `sha256.Sum256` of it (`history.go:398`), a second hash into `generationHash` (`history.go:402`), the staged write (`history.go:412`), a third hash via `historyIndexBytesFingerprint` (`history.go:430`), and `historyRecordsFingerprint` (`history.go:431`, body at `history.go:1141`) which re-marshals all 168171 records one at a time. There is no HEAD-keyed early-out inside `refresh history` — it always rebuilds; the only skip guard, `historyIndexCurrent` (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/refresh.go:554`), is used solely by the full `refresh` (`refresh.go:298`) and is itself expensive because `collectHistorySessionDigests` (`history.go:1417-1438`) reads and hashes the whole corpus a third time. Old generations are pruned correctly (`history.go:550-558` → `pruneInactiveHistoryGenerations`, `history.go:676`), so disk does not grow unbounded. Fixes: stream-encode the index straight to the staged file through an `io.MultiWriter` that computes both digests in one pass, drop `MarshalIndent` for a machine-read artifact, derive `RecordsFingerprint` incrementally from the per-file cached digests, and reuse the build's digests for the post-scan identity check instead of re-reading the corpus.

### 3. `entities history` spends its 61s on the same full checkpoint-store scan, and does it even when the entity index is empty

`entityHistory` → `loadEntityIndexView` (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/entities_cmd.go:573`) ends every path — cache hit, cache miss, stale-cache fallback — through the `finish` closure at `entities_cmd.go:591`, which unconditionally calls `sessionIDsByCheckpoint` (`entities_cmd.go:853`). That function calls `loadLocalCheckpointSnapshotForVerify` at `entities_cmd.go:868` — the exact scan from my earlier finding: one `git ls-tree` per checkpoint ref plus one `git cat-file` per metadata blob, serially, with the metadata cache passed as `nil`. With the graph plugin missing, `rebuildEntityIndexCache` returns at `entities_cmd.go:671-673` (`snapshot.Empty()`) with zero entries, so the join loop at `entities_cmd.go:598-603` iterates nothing — the entire snapshot was built to populate a map that is then applied to an empty set. A smaller add-on: `entityindex.ProviderIdentity` at `entities_cmd.go:606` shells `entire graph version --json` under a 10s timeout (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/entityindex/identity.go:28-30`), which is wasted work when the plugin is absent. Fix: return early from `finish` when `view.cache.Entries` is empty, and otherwise pass the set of checkpoint IDs actually referenced by the entries so the snapshot load can be scoped instead of enumerating the whole store.

### 4. This plugin never runs `git remote -v` — but every git call it *does* make spawns a second, uncached `git config` probe

Exhaustive search of the production Go code turns up exactly three remote-related git spawns, none of them `-v`: `git remote get-url origin` at `/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/env.go:409` and `/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/add.go:61`, and `git config --get-regexp ^remote\..*\.url$` at `/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/semantic_repokey.go:98`. The only `git remote -v` strings in the tree are recorded agent bash commands inside `benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/.../record.json`, i.e. transcripts of an agent running it itself — that is the likely source of the 105 orphans, not this plugin. content.text:
All benchmarking and root-cause work is complete. Full data is in `.context/bench/results.csv`; findings are recorded as durable Brain facts. Here's the ranked list.

## Ranked performance problems

All slow paths scale with **retained checkpoint/session volume**, not repo size — a 12GB repo with no sessions cold-indexes in 28s, while this repo's 337-transcript/1.5GB store makes "cheap" commands take a minute. Everything was measured on real stores across 5 states (big-indexed, un-indexed, fresh-small, fresh-medium, stale), with root causes confirmed in source.

**1. `status` takes 60–72s, every run (also `brain_status` over MCP: 72s)** — the worst because it's the entry point everything tells agents to run, and 72s blows past typical 60s MCP tool timeouts. `brief` proves the base report costs 0.3s; the rest is `populateBrainStatusVerification` loading the *entire* checkpoint store: one serial `git ls-tree` per checkpoint ref plus one `git cat-file` per metadata blob (`internal/cli/export.go:1705-2800`). A metadata cache exists (`export/checkpoint-metadata-cache.json.gz`) but this path passes `nil` for it (`verify_cmd.go:798`) — wiring it in is nearly a one-line fix. Snapshot assembly is also O(checkpoints × tree-paths) (`export.go:2062`). Fix: pass the cache, batch blobs through one `git cat-file --batch`, scope the snapshot to the 10 sampled facts' checkpoints.

**2. `verify` takes 334s for 1211 facts** — per anchor it runs `git for-each-ref --contains` (an O(history) walk, memoized only per commit, and each fact tends to have its own commit) plus **two full transcript reads with no memoization** — ~10GB of redundant I/O since facts share sessions (`verify_cmd.go:381-523,674`). Fix: batch reachability once for all distinct commits, memoize transcripts on the context, compare digests instead of full bytes.

**3. `refresh delta` takes 39–47s even when there's nothing to do** — this is your "slow indexing at startup," since hooks/watch run delta routinely. It reads and SHA-256s the whole 1.5GB corpus *before* the size+mtime cache check can short-circuit, because the check requires the digest it was supposed to avoid computing (`history_delta.go:307-334`, `history.go:1449`). Fix: hash only when size/mtime differ. The export half is fine (`refresh sessions` alone: 0.8s).

**4. `refresh history` takes 48s and always rebuilds all 168k records** — it hashes the corpus twice more, and materializes the 113MB index roughly four times (`MarshalIndent`, three separate hashes, per-record re-marshal for the fingerprint) (`history.go:363-431`). The only skip-guard re-hashes the corpus a third time. Side effect: the first read of the 113MB index makes the next `brief` spike to 5.7s (0.4s warm). Fix: stream-encode once through a MultiWriter computing both digests; derive fingerprints from cached per-file digests.

**5. `entities history` takes 61s to return nothing** — every path through `loadEntityIndexView` runs the same full checkpoint scan as #1 (again with `nil` cache), even when the entity index is empty because the graph plugin is missing; plus a wasted 10s-timeout `entire graph version` probe (`entities_cmd.go:591-868`). Fix: early-return on empty index; scope the snapshot to referenced checkpoints.

**6. Amplifier: every git call spawns a second, uncached `git config` probe** (`runner.go:88`, `git_harden_filters.go:85-124`), doubling the fork bill on findings 1/2/5 — ~27s of the status run is sys time from fork/exec. It's also the one spawn with no `WaitDelay`. A per-invocation memo halves process count everywhere at once.

**7. Semantic indexing couldn't be measured here** — `refresh index`, `repair`, and `entities backfill` all fail because entire-graph isn't installed on this machine, so the historically recorded worst offender (provider snapshot timing out at 900s, per Brain's own recall) is unverified in this audit. Worth a follow-up run on a machine with the graph plugin.

## What's already fast (no action)

`query` all modes ~0.2s, `brief` 0.35s, `recall` 0.24s, `get`/`multi-get`, `stats`, `doctor`, `gc`, `remember`, `facts vitality`, `overview`, `docs`, MCP initialize/tools-list/query (0.1–0.2s). Un-indexed repos fail fast (0.2s). Cold non-semantic indexing is fine: 4s small / 5s medium / 28s for the 12GB repo. History generations are pruned correctly — no unbounded disk growth.

## Side findings

- ~105 `git remote -v` processes, 5 days old, orphaned to launchd on your machine. **Not brain's code** (it never runs `remote -v`; its runner is leak-safe) — they match agent-transcript commands, so some agent harness is leaking them. Worth a `pkill -f 'git remote -v'`.
- `refresh --agent none` exits 1 on a dirty worktree with the error only on stderr — in scripts it looks like a silent failure; needs `--worktree`.
- Not tested (interactive/mutating/needs-agent): `distill`, `publish`, `webhook`, `dash`, `viz`, `watch`, `setup` daemon install, `facts sync`/`proposals`.

**Biggest wins by effort:** wire the existing metadata cache into status/verify/entities (near one-line, kills most of #1/#5) and gate delta's hashing on size+mtime (kills #3). Those two alone take the worst everyday paths from ~45–70s to roughly nothing.
